title: The Obedience of Christ
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The obedience of Christ means that Jesus perfectly fulfilled the Father’s will in every thought, desire, word, action, suffering, and sacrifice. He obeyed where sinners failed and accomplished righteousness for His people.
summary: The obedience of Christ means that Jesus perfectly fulfilled the Father’s will in every thought, desire, word, action, suffering, and sacrifice. He obeyed where sinners failed and accomplished righteousness for His people.
christFocus: Jesus is the obedient Son who came not to do His own will but the will of the Father. His obedience leads to the cross and secures righteousness and life for those who belong to Him.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Jesus lived in perfect obedience to the Father. He did not merely avoid outward sin; He loved, trusted, worshiped, and obeyed God from the heart without failure.

His obedience is seen throughout His life and especially in His suffering. In Gethsemane and at the cross, He submitted to the Father’s will even when obedience meant agony and death.

Christ’s obedience answers Adam’s disobedience. Through the disobedience of one man many were made sinners, but through the obedience of Christ many are made righteous.

The obedience of Christ is central to salvation. He fulfills righteousness, obeys the law, suffers as the obedient Son, and becomes the source of eternal salvation to all who obey Him in faith.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People often think salvation is only about forgiveness of past sins. But sinners also need righteousness before God. Christ’s obedience provides what sinners could never produce for themselves.

This doctrine also teaches discipleship. Believers are not saved by their obedience, but they are saved by the obedient Christ who then calls them to follow Him in obedience.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Rest in the obedience of Christ rather than your own record. Then follow Him with gratitude, especially when obedience is costly. Pray for a heart that says with Christ, “Not my will, but yours be done.”
